subject: Multi-region Dedicated — replication, DR, and commit structure

Subject: Multi-region Dedicated capacity — replication/DR options

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for taking our call last week. As we start to put numbers into the RFP, procurement and infra have a few concrete questions about Redwood Dedicated for a multi-region rollout. High level: AvaTech plans to serve low-latency assistants from US and EU regions with APAC as a DR/latency-optimized region.

Specific asks:
- We expect baseline sustained load of ~600 concurrent sessions in US (median 128 tokens/session/min). EU will start smaller (~250 concurrent). APAC initially 50.
- We want a clear pricing model for separate pools per region (preferred) vs a single pooled cross-region capacity.
- Replication/DR options: active-active (geo-shard + sync KV), active-passive warm spare, and cold standby. What are cost deltas and RTO/RPO you can guarantee?
- Throughput guarantees: can you commit to a per-region throughput SLA (tokens/sec or rps) for reserved pools, including burst behavior?
- Cross-region routing and egress: any additional fees when traffic fails over from US -> EU or vice versa?
- Reserved commit lengths: 12mo vs 24mo pricing tiers and discount levels we can quote to procurement.

I attached the RFP draft for context. Procurement wants a high-level term sheet and an example price for the configuration below so we can model TCO:
- US-west pool: target equivalent of 8x A100 (sustained)
- EU-west pool: 4x A100
- APAC pool: 2x A100 (DR)

Can you send a short term sheet and an estimate by EOD Tuesday?

Best,
Elena Morales

Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated capacity — replication/DR options

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks and the RFP. I outlined the options below and attached a draft term sheet that maps to the three replication models. Quick summary first, then numbers/examples for the config you listed.

Summary of replication/DR models:
- Active-active (recommended if you need minimal failover latency): each region owns a portion of traffic (geo-shard). KV/prefix caching can be replicated; cross-region synchronization is best-effort for cache metadata, model state is replicated to same model version in each region. Pricing: active-active adds an approximate 18% premium over the sum of per-region reserved commits to cover inter-region replication bandwidth and capacity overhead. RTO: <20s in most routes; RPO: seconds for KV, immediate for model binaries (already resident).

- Active-passive (warm spare): primary region handles traffic, passive region keeps warmed model cache and standby GPU capacity scaled to 30–50% of primary. Promotion is automatic with targeted 60–120s cutover depending on session rehydration. Pricing: ~8–10% premium over base reserved commits.

- Cold standby: model binaries staged but not warmed; cold boot on failover (RTO measured in minutes). Pricing: no premium beyond standard pay-as-you-go bursts and egress fees.

Pricing structure (reserved commits):
- Base unit: A100-month equivalent (we price per A100-month for simplicity).
- Example discounts: 12-month commit = 20% off list; 24-month commit = 30% off list. Additional migration / replication premium applies per the model chosen.

Example for your requested sizing (list prices redacted to keep this email short; see attached term sheet for full numbers):
- US-west: 8x A100 (recommended 12-month commit) -> base commit price applies; active-passive premium would add ~8%
- EU-west: 4x A100 -> separate commit; cross-region routing configured with primary in US for latency-sensitive traffic
- APAC: 2x A100 as warm-DR (cold standby option also available)

Throughput guarantees and SLAs:
- We can commit to a per-pool throughput target expressed as concurrent-session capacity and 99.9th percentile per-token latency SLO for reserved pools. Example: 8x A100 pool can be committed to support 600 concurrent short-context sessions at X tokens/sec (see term sheet for numbers derived from model profile). Bursts beyond commit handled by autoscaling burst window (configurable) — charges apply for burst usage above commit.

Cross-region egress and routing:
- Inter-region failover traffic is charged at a discounted transfer rate for Reserved customers (we apply a replication allowance tied to commit size; extras billed at egress rates).

Next steps: Dev, can you attach a short design note for replication mechanics and an internal sizing note? Elena — I attached a term sheet draft (Redwood_Dedicated_MultiRegion_TermSheet_v3.pdf) with a line-item estimate. Happy to hop on a 30-min call Tuesday if you want to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Elena — quick technical addendum to Ben's note to make sure procurement models the right operational guarantees.

1) Throughput/Concurrency mapping: we size reserved pools against two axes: concurrent sessions (long-lived) and peak token throughput (short bursts). For your stated workloads (600 concurrent US), the 8x A100 recommendation assumes average seq len 256 tokens and a 1.5x headroom for peaks. We express SLA as: 'Reserved pool supports N concurrent sessions at P tokens/sec with 99.9% availability.'

2) Warm replication details:
- KV/prefix cache: optional async replication. Warm spare keeps model binaries resident and a warmed KV snapshot; rehydration of active session state requires prefix replay for sessions older than snapshot.
- Active-active constraints: cross-region KV sync will increase tail latency under heavy write load. We recommend active-active only if you can tolerate occasional 5–10% tail latency variation during high write windows.

3) Autoscale & burst: Reserved pools include a burst bucket (configurable) that auto-scales for short spikes (we bill bursts separately). If you need guaranteed sustained bursting, we need to size commit higher.

4) Data residency & logging: Audit logs and request traces stay in the owning region by default; cross-region failover will replicate only the minimum necessary metadata unless you opt into cross-region telemetry replication (additional fee).

I attached a short design doc that shows replication flow and expected RTO/RPO by model. Happy to jump on a technical call with your infra team.

— Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Can you provide the committed pricing lines (A100-month price) for 12mo and 24mo so we can compare to other vendors? A simple table is fine.
2) SLA credits: procurement wants explicit language on how credits are calculated for cross-region outages and whether credits are capped per month.
3) DocuSign + DPA: we need a signed DPA and prefer DocuSign-ready term sheet. Can you indicate which DPA template you use and whether you accept edits on data retention periods?

Also, for the APAC DR pool — if we choose cold-standby initially, what's an estimate of warm-up time to get to production-ready (session rehydration + model warm)? We need that number for our runbook.

If you can get those items back to us by EOD Thursday we can push this into our legal queue.

Elena

Elena —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Attached is an updated term sheet with explicit 12/24 month A100-month line items and an SLA credits section that spells out calculation and monthly caps. Quick answers inline below and doc links are at the bottom.

1) Committed pricing lines: included in the term sheet (see 'Pricing Summary' page). For modeling purposes, example (round numbers): 12-mo A100-month = $XX, 24-mo A100-month = $YY (24mo reflects ~30% off list). The term sheet has full line items per region and the replication premiums for active-active / active-passive.

2) SLA credits: we propose a tiered credit system — regional outage affecting >5% of requests for a billing month triggers credits pro-rated to impacted pool commit, capped at 50% of monthly committed spend for that pool. Cross-region failover that preserves availability (within RTO) does not trigger credit unless SLOs are missed. Full language in term sheet.

3) DPA & DocuSign: we use the standard Redwood DPA (link in doc). We can accept reasonable edits to data retention windows — major changes will require legal review but we typically accept firm-specific retention clauses for enterprise deals. I included a DocuSign-ready term sheet link: https://docusign.com/xyz/AVT-RD-87

4) APAC cold -> warm: cold-to-warm warmup (model binaries resident + KV snapshot applied) typically ~6–10 minutes for model family similar to the one in your RFP. Full session rehydration depends on session age; if you want session-level continuity we recommend warm spare.

Next steps:
- If procurement is comfortable with the attached term sheet I can generate a DocuSign envelope and loop in legal.
- We can schedule a short runbook / ops workshop to validate the warm failover steps and cutover windows.

Would you like us to produce a short cost comparison table against a pooled single-capacity approach (one shared global pool) vs separate per-region commits? We can include that in the final package.

Best,
Ben Carter
